div.head: Af 32
div.ab: XXVIIII. Gif mon folcleasunge gewyrce, ⁊ heo on hine geræf weorðe, mid nanum leohtran ðinge gebete þonne him mon aceorfe ða tungan of, ðæt hy món nó undeorran weorðe moste alysan, ðonne mon be þæm were geeahtige.

XXVIIII. Gif mon folcleasunge gewyrce, ⁊ hio on hine geresp weorðe, mid nanum leohtran ðinge gebete þonne him mon aceorfe þa tungon óf, þæt hie mon na undeorran weorðe moste lesan, ðonne hie mon be þam were geeahtige.
Si quis publicum mendacium confingat, et in ipsum denique firmetur, non emendetur hoc aliqua levi re, sed amputetur ei lingua, nec minori pretio redimi possit quam secundum weram eius adpreciabitur.

{XXVIIII} Gif mon folcleasunge gewyrce, ⁊ hio on hine geresp weorðe, mid nanum leohtran ðinge gebete þonne him mon aceorfe þa tungon óf, þæt hie mon na undeorran weorðe moste lesan, ðonne hie mon be þam were geeahtige.

If someone engages in public slander, and he is convicted of it, let him pay with no lighter settlement than that one should cut out his tongue, nor shall it be redeemed for a lesser worth than is reckoned according to his wer.

If anyone utter a public slander, and it is proved against him, he shall make amends on no lighter terms than the excision of his tongue [with the provision that] it shall not be ransomed at a cheaper price than [its value], estimated according to the man's wergeld.

If anyone is guilty of public slander, and it is proved against him, it is to be compensated for with no lighter penalty than the cutting off of his tongue, with the proviso that it be redeemed at no cheaper rate than it is valued in proportion to the wergild.

Wenn jemand öffentliche Verleumdung bewirkt, und sie auf ihm Schuldbelastung wird, so büsse er mit keinem leichteren Dinge, als [dass] man ihm die Zunge abschneide, [so] dass er sie nicht um billigeren Preis auslösen könne, als man sie je nach dem Wergeld [des Verleumders] schätzt.

If someone commits public slander, and it becomes a charge of guilt upon him, let him pay with nothing lighter than [that] his tongue be cut out, [so] that he could not redeem it at a cheaper price than it is valued according to [the slanderer’s] wergeld.
